passage:
Tuesday
At dinner I said maybe I want commerce, not science. Appa didn't even look up. 'You'll understand when you're older.' Amma nodded. That's it. That's what they say about everything: my haircut, my friends, even debate club. So I've stopped telling them things. I didn't mention I got selected for the district debate. I told Amma the practice sessions were extra maths.
Tonight Vidya Akka found the certificate in my bag and asked why I'm hiding it. I said, 'What's the point? I'll understand when I'm older.' She didn't argue. She said she used to do the same, and it made everything worse later. I don't know. I just want one conversation where they actually listen.
Jeevan

qa.q: What did Vidya Akka find in Jeevan's bag?
What does Jeevan feel about hearing 'You'll understand when you're older'?
qa.a: Jeevan feels unheard and frustrated, as if every opinion gets shut down, which has led to hiding things.

qa.q: What could help rebuild trust in this family?
qa.a: Jeevan could share the debate news with Vidya Akka's support, and Appa and Amma could ask about the commerce idea and truly listen instead of closing it.

qa.q: How might Vidya Akka see Jeevan's hiding?
qa.a: Vidya Akka recognises the pattern and seems worried, because hiding things once made life harder for her too.

grounding: Shows a teenager whose opinions are shut down with 'you'll understand when you're older', who goes quiet and hides things, harming trust on both sides.

Farhan: maybe. but at least you said it properly 🤞
Aditi: ...ok. tomorrow.
